intro: Professionals and everyday users convert bars (bar) to megapascals (MPa) when working across metric and si standards in automotive tire inflation placards, hydraulic cylinder design, scuba diving tanks, and barometric weather tracking. One bar equals 0.1 megapascals, while 1 megapascal equals 10 bars. Whether you are verifying pressure specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Gauge Pressure (psig) vs. Absolute Pressure (psia)
items: This converter scales pressure magnitude directly between bar and MPa. In automotive tires, HVAC, and compressed air systems, gauges display Gauge Pressure (referenced to ambient atmospheric pressure, ~14.696 psi or 101.325 kPa at sea level).
For thermodynamic gas laws (PV = nRT) or vacuum chamber calculations, convert gauge pressure to absolute pressure by adding local barometric pressure before scaling.

faqs.question: How many megapascals (MPa) are in 1 bar (bar)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.1 megapascals (MPa) in 1 bar (bar), which rounds to 0.1 MPa for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 megapascal equals 10 bars.

faqs.question: How do I convert bars to megapascals (bar to MPa)?
faqs.answer: To convert bars to megapascals, use the formula: MPa = bar × 0.1. For example, converting 2.2 bar gives 0.22 MPa.

faqs.question: What is 2.2 bars in megapascals?
faqs.answer: 2.2 bars (bar) equals exactly 0.22 megapascals (MPa) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
